_about: Working stage scenario, still subject to site-plan and product changes; do not build logic or default copy around its details. This seeded MOCK/DEMO_MODE run uses fictional organiser names, contact details, suppliers and arrangements for demonstration only. It is not an actual application or evidence that a special licence has been granted. Every key is validated by tests/contract.test.ts. Council rules and checklists for live events come from verified knowledge, not this fixture.
description: Hagley Summer Sounds is a music festival at Hagley Park on Sunday 14 March, 12 till 9pm. Around 500 people, all ages welcome, with a kids zone and a bouncy castle. Live music from local bands on a main stage, a bar selling beer and wine to over 18s, four food trucks, and a couple of marquees for shade.

questions.question: How big is your largest marquee?

classification.reasoning: The council source lists community and commercial fee bands for Hagley Park but does not define which applies here. A music festival with a bar and food trucks could fall in either band, depending on who runs it and where the takings go.
classification.howToPresent: Explain who runs the festival, whether it is free or ticketed, where any profit goes, and how much of the site is commercial trading; ask the council to confirm the category before quoting a fee.

sections.heading: Event overview
sections.body: DEMO ONLY. Hagley Summer Sounds is a proposed all-ages music festival at Hagley Park on Sunday 14 March 2027, 12pm to 9pm, with an expected peak of 500 people including children. Beer and wine sales are planned at a fenced bar for over 18s, subject to a special licence being granted.

sections.heading: Key hazards and controls
sections.body: Main stage and sound equipment, built and signed off by Demo Stage Hire (fictional demo contractor), with the front of stage barriered and cables covered. Inflatable bouncy castle in the kids zone, anchored to manufacturer specification and supervised by Sam Example (fictional demo volunteer). Generators for the stage and food trucks, fenced and away from public areas. If licensed, alcohol sales will be confined to the fenced bar with a duty manager present.

sections.heading: Emergency response
sections.body: First aid tent beside the main entrance, staffed from 11.30am until the site is clear. In an evacuation, the stage announces it over the PA and marshals direct attendees through the north and east exits to [ASSEMBLY POINT].

sections.heading: Roles and contacts
sections.body: Event manager Jordan Example; proposed duty manager Taylor Example; first aid provider Demo First Aid Crew. All are fictional demo assignments to verify before lodging.

sections.heading: Bins and recycling
sections.body: Rubbish and recycling bins at the bar, beside each of the four food trucks, in the kids zone and at both entrances. Cups at the bar are reusable, with a return point beside it.

sections.heading: During and after the event
sections.body: Volunteers empty bins during the event and walk the site for litter after close at 9pm. Demo Waste Services (fictional demo contractor) is assigned to remove the waste that night.

sections.heading: Inflatable bouncy castle
sections.body: Risk: falls, collisions and the castle lifting in wind. Proposed controls: anchored to manufacturer specification, supervised by Sam Example (fictional demo volunteer), age and number limits posted, deflated if the wind picks up. Residual risk: to be confirmed on site.

sections.heading: Stage, sound and crowd at the front
sections.body: Risk: crushing at the front of stage, hearing damage and trips on cables. Controls: barrier along the front of stage, sound levels monitored at the mixing desk, cables covered and taped. Residual risk: low.

sections.heading: Generators and food truck cooking
sections.body: Risk: burns, fire and fuel spills. Controls: generators fenced off from the public, fire extinguisher at each food truck, gas bottles secured upright. Residual risk: low.

sections.heading: Alcohol
sections.body: Risk: intoxication and under-18s being served. If a special licence is granted, proposed controls are sales only inside the fenced bar, duty manager Taylor Example (fictional demo assignment) on site, and ID checks at the bar entrance. Residual risk: to be confirmed on site.

sections.heading: Crowd and lost children
sections.body: Risk: crowding at the busiest time (about 500 people) and children getting separated. Controls: marshals at both entrances, lost child point at the first aid tent. Residual risk: low.

sections.body: Hagley Summer Sounds at Hagley Park on Sunday 14 March 2027. Proposed beer and wine sales are limited to a fenced bar for over 18s, 12pm to 8.30pm, only if a special licence is granted. The exact licensed boundary must match the site plan.

sections.heading: Duty manager
sections.body: Proposed duty manager Taylor Example is a fictional demo assignment for the 12pm to 8.30pm sales period. Manager certification must be verified before a real application is lodged.

sections.heading: Host responsibility
sections.body: The plan has four food trucks trading throughout proposed alcohol sales, with free water and non-alcoholic drinks at the bar. Staff will check ID at the bar entrance. The fictional demo transport plan provides a marked taxi and rideshare pickup at the park edge and public-transport information at the exit.

sections.heading: Type of event
sections.body: DEMO ONLY. Proposed all-ages music festival, about 500 people at peak including children. Beer and wine sales at a fenced bar for over 18s are planned only if a special licence is granted. Event manager Jordan Example is in charge overall; proposed duty manager Taylor Example is in charge of the bar. Both are fictional demo assignments.

sections.heading: Promoting your event
sections.body: Promotion states the festival is all ages, that intoxicated people will be refused service and removed, that no alcohol may be brought in, and that ID is checked at the bar.

sections.heading: Intoxication
sections.body: If licensed, bar staff and the duty manager will monitor patrons and intervene early. Intoxicated people will be refused entry. The fictional demo welfare point is a quiet tent beside first aid.

sections.heading: Food
sections.body: Four food trucks are planned to trade throughout alcohol sales. Jordan Example (fictional demo manager) will check that food stays available; if it runs out, alcohol sales stop.

sections.heading: Low and non-alcohol beverages
sections.body: Low-alcohol beer, soft drinks and free water are available and promoted at the bar at all times.

sections.heading: Minors
sections.body: Photo ID (NZ driver licence, passport or 18+ card) is checked for anyone who appears under 25.

sections.heading: Signage
sections.body: If granted, the special licence will be displayed at the bar with required signage at each point of sale. Jordan Example (fictional demo manager) will put up the signs.

sections.heading: Safe transport
sections.body: The fictional demo plan marks a taxi and rideshare pickup at the park edge and gives public-transport information at the exit. Staff will offer alternatives to anyone who has been drinking and intends to drive.

sections.heading: Alcohol promotions on the day
sections.body: No discounts, drinking games or alcohol prizes. Last drinks are called at 8.30pm, half an hour before the music stops.

sections.heading: Staff training
sections.body: All bar staff and volunteers are briefed on the licence conditions and this plan before the event.

sections.heading: Incident and noting book
sections.body: The duty manager records refusals, removals and incidents in an incident book kept at the bar.

sections.heading: Security
sections.body: The fictional demo plan assigns four staff from Demo Event Security, 11am to 10pm, covering both entrances, the bar and the front of stage, with Jordan Example as liaison. A real provider, staffing level and qualifications must be confirmed before lodging.

sections.heading: Environment
sections.body: Seating and shade in the marquees near the bar, the kids zone kept well away from it, and toilets available throughout.

sections.heading: Debriefing
sections.body: Staff and contractors debrief after the event to note improvements.

deadlines.label: Lodge event permit application with site plan and health and safety plan
deadlines.basis: CCC processing starts at five weeks for a low impact event. We aim for ten weeks.

deadlines.label: Lodge special licence application
deadlines.basis: At least 20 working days before the event. 20 Dec to 15 Jan does not count. We aim two weeks earlier.

deadlines.label: Attach alcohol management plan to special licence application
deadlines.basis: The alcohol management plan is an attachment to the special licence application, so it shares that lodgement date.

deadlines.label: Provide site plan to CCC
deadlines.basis: CCC's conditions for events on public land require this plan at least six weeks before the event.
